ideas.title: My first motor boat: a self-starting motor on a raft turns a paddle wheel
ideas.critique: This is round 2's self-starting motor with the jet and sail taken out, which removes the weakest link. Paddle thrust on the real blade area meets the motor's torque, and the hull trims under the friend's weight, so the build is something a player tunes and carries forward. The risk is the same as before: the motor never truly ran in its own post. It also stacks four new solvers (N-pole motor, paddle forces, buoyancy, ripples), so a session may end with a raft nudged by a fitted constant, filmed like one more lone device on water.

ideas.title: My beak grips by friction and my body carries the weight
ideas.critique: This is round 2's 'My beak carries the weight' with friction added, and the friction is the real step: a smooth iron nail slipping out while a rough stone of the same weight holds is an outcome the body works out for itself, not a pose. The danger is that a SIMBICON-style balance controller with Hill-curve neck torques is a research project. The likeliest first version is an IK head with a scripted dip, and the slip-out could turn into a threshold on a number.

ideas.title: The friends heave my cart up the dune
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Turning round 2's downhill roll into an uphill heave helps a lot. Pushes capped by foot traction, with feet slipping and the cart stalling, make the friends work against the physics, and widening the wheels is a fix the player chooses. What's weak is that 'friends heave a cart' without a motor skips the road's own core, and the stall-then-crest arc can easily be staged. The friends' locomotion pushing with real forces is untested, and it is the part most likely to quietly become scripted.
